PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting a
meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the individual ’s
failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

  CONSENT CALENDAR

no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed

minutes_text:
AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called the meeting to order at 5:07 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items on the closed session agenda. 

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION City Council/Successor Agency recessed to Closed Session at 5:08 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council/Successor Agency reconvened to Open Session at 6:06 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed session items:

Items #1 and #2 - Staff made a presentation, the City Council provided direction and no reportable action was taken on any of these items.  

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called regular City Council meeting to order at 6:08 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Deputy Director of Public Works Operations led the Pledge of Allegiance

INVOCATION Mayor Argumedo offered the invocation.

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

1.. Tree City U.S.A. 2023 Award and Recognition of the Arbor Day 2024 Poster Contest Winners Mark Martinez, Deputy Forester with the LA County Fire Department, discussed the criteria for the City's achievements and highlighted its consistent recognition as a Tree City USA for 28 consecutive years. Nick Padilla, Park Maintenance Leadworker, and the Rosewood School Principal presented awards to the contest winners.

3.. Presentation on the 2024 Summer Reading Program and the Update on the Library of Things Collection Silvia Cisneros, Senior Librarian, provided an overview of the summer reading program. Edward Hernandez, Technical Services Supervisor, announced that the Library received another grant, which funded 25 solar portable chargers, and he conducted a demonstration of these chargers.

2.. Certificate of Recognition for the Commerce Evening Lions Club for their Contributions, and Outstanding Volunteerism This item was continued to the next City Council meeting. 

PUBLIC COMMENT 
Jose Cruz, Nadine Huacuja, Jesus Huacuja, and Andrea McCormick, parents of water polo team members, advocated for cultural excursions for the team. Billy Cruz, Rodrigo Mena, and Nathan Martinez also supported allowing the boys' water polo team to participate in cultural excursions to enhance their skills.



Omar Torrones expressed gratitude for the generosity of the sponsors and thanked Councilmembers Rebollo and Lainez for their year-end assistance, as well as all sponsors who contributed to the Renaissance group. 
Mayra Huerta thanked everyone for supporting youth groups, acknowledging donations and assistance that helped the Renaissance group achieve their goals. She also expressed appreciation for the Teen Center staff, Councilmember Rebollo for inspiring the youth, Councilmember Lainez for his proactive support, Mayor Argumedo for his prompt action, and the teachers at Rosewood Park.



Gloria Nezahualcoyotl made a statement for the record.

A brief discussion ensued regarding travel guidelines and ensuring fairness for all groups seeking cultural excursions.




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo City Manager Hernandez requested that item #7 is continued to the next City Council meeting.  Councilmember Lainez asked to pull item #6 for discussion.  

item #6 - Councilmember Lainez inquired about the timeline for the design. Deputy Director of Public Works Operations, Nila, responded that there is no established timeline yet but estimated it would take about six months. Councilmember Lainez emphasized the importance of community outreach and sought assurance that it would be conducted, asking for thoughts on how to gather feedback. He also suggested obtaining input from staff working in the facility regarding the functionality of room designs. Deputy Director Nila mentioned that community feedback received during the creation of Parks Master Paln would also be incorporated.

Councilmember Rebollo moved, seconded by Councilmember Lainez, to adopt a Resolution approving a Professional Service Agreement with John G. Cataldo Architect, A.I.A. C.S.I. Architect, Inc. to provide professional services to prepare Plans, Specifications, and Engineer’s Estimate for the Renovation of Bristow Park Community Center and Library; authorizing Transtech Engineers, Inc. to proceed with the Project and allocating $267,851.50 in Measure AA funding to cover the total project cost.  The motion was carried by the following vote: 

AYES: Councilmembers Garcia, Lainez, Rebollo, Vice Mayor Altamirano and Mayor Argumedo (5)

6.. Bristow Park Community Center and Library Renovation - Approval of Professional Services Agreement with John G. Cataldo

5.. Approval of Minutes

7.. First Amendment to Assistant City Manager Employment Agreement Between Vilko Domic and the City of Commerce

SCHEDULED MATTERS

8.. PRESENTATION/UPDATE FROM THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY IN THE CITY OF COMMERCE Sergeant Duarte provided an overview of the past two weeks and mentioned that the next report will include additional statistics requested by the Council.








9.. Resolution by the City Council Re-Naming a Portion of Tubeway Avenue after Haig Papaian, former Commerce Casino CEO and President  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo Assistant City Manager Domic provided an overview, mentioning that there is a second alternative in which Commerce Casino wants to vacate Tubeway. The current suggestion of renaming Tubeway would affect four businesses, including their mailing addresses, whereas the second alternative would not impact any businesses.



A discussion ensued. City Manager Hernandez suggested that the renaming ceremony could take place at the current street location and later be moved to the new realignment. Councilmember Rebollo recommended that staff check with Haig Papian’s family on whether to name the street "Haig Papian Jr. Way" or simply "Haig Papian Way."

ORDINANCES

10.. Adoption of Urgency Ordinance Amending Commerce Municipal Code, Chapter 5.10 (“Use and Sale of Safe and Sane Fireworks”) of Title 5 and Adding a New Chapter 16.05 to Title 16 Prohibiting the Possession, Sale, and/or Discharge of Dangerous Fireworks and Establishing Penalties; and Introduction of Ordinance Amending Municipal Code Chapter 5.10 (“Use and Sale of Safe and Sane Fireworks”) of Tile 5 and Adding a New Chapter 16.05 to Title 16 Prohibiting the Possession, Sale, and/or Discharge of Dangerous Fireworks and Establish Penalties (First Reading)  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez 
City Attorney Tapia provided a brief overview.

In response to Councilmember Lainez's inquiry about the enforcement of the ordinance, City Manager Hernandez explained that the plan is to educate the public. He noted that the Commerce Team is aware of certain hot spots and violators and will be conducting enforcement and preventive measures in advance.



Councilmember Rebollo emphasized the importance of community awareness, urging residents to consider the impact of noise on infants, military personnel, and pets, who are particularly sensitive. 

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Garcia visited  the East Los Angeles Women's Shelter Team and toured a shelter in Commerce. Councilmember also attended a football clinic at Rosewood Park and attended the swearing-in ceremony at the Metropolitan Water District where Jim Crowford was sworn in as a board member. Additionally, Councilmember Garcia attended the Schurr High School graduation ceremony, congratulating the Class of 2024 graduates.



Councilmember Rebollo congratulated the Class of 2024 graduates and thanked Social Services Coordinator garcia for the College Banners for class 2024. Councilmember Rebollo also congratulated the Water Polo teams that qualified for the Junior Olympics in San Jose in July and noted that volleyball and baseball try-outs are going on.



Councilmember Lainez stated that he is also a board member of the Gateway Cities Affordable Housing Trust, highlighted that they started review of project applications and funding for affordable housing this year. Councilmember Lainez reported that he attended the Bell Chamber of Commerce anniversary, and congratulated Janine Andrade for receiving the Community Service Award and Matt Johnson for receiving the Prestigious Distinguished Award.  Councilmember Lainez also reported attending Jim Crowford's swearing-in ceremony at the Metropolitan Water District, the Rosewood 8th-grade banquet where he was impressed by advocacy and fundraising efforts, and the Veil High School graduation at Bell Gardens High School, congratulating all the graduates.



Mayor Argumedo congratulated the Class of 2024 graduates and stated that he attended Veil High School's graduation. Mayor Argumedo reported attending a "Day at the Races" event with the Vice Mayor and an Evening Lions Club meeting. Mayor Argumedo requested staff to investigate the use of Camp Commerce and the beach area at Lake Arrowhead, suggesting that the City cover fees for patrons. He also asked staff to explore the installation of stoplights with cameras for issuing citations.  Mayor Argumedo asked that staff provide status update on priority projects, requesting status updates, identification of issues, and problem resolution.

ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 7:54 p.m.

Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings) in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California, and the Central Library, 5655 Jillson Street, Commerce, California.


Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.
